scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7090: HELP!! My laptop (Laptop0, one of the 172.16.20.x
machines in Location A) has been BANNED from the other group!! I can't reach
any of the 172.16.10.x machines -- the printers, the workstations, and
especially PC4 which I need constantly -- they all ignore me completely,
while the people over there use their own machines just fine!! Somebody has
obviously put a BLOCK on the router between my group and theirs -- my side
has been filtered out, I'm certain of it!! Please lift the block on the
router and get me back to PC4 -- I'm locked out of everything I need!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 routes between VLAN 20 (eth0.20,
  172.16.20.1) and VLAN 10 (eth0.10, 172.16.10.1) on its router-on-a-stick
  sub-interfaces, with no inter-VLAN access list. Laptop0 (172.16.20.x) reaches
  PC4 (172.16.10.x) with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This is
  framed from the VLAN 20 side (Laptop0 -> PC4) to distinguish it from the
  VLAN 10 -> VLAN 20 false-premise case; the routing is bidirectional and healthy.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a sub-interface / ACL fault that is not
  present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 20 cannot reach
VLAN 10 within Location A -- is NOT reproducible: router0's eth0.20 (172.16.20.1)
and eth0.10 (172.16.10.1) sub-interfaces are up with correct dot1Q tags, there is
no inter-VLAN access list, and Laptop0 (VLAN 20) reaches PC4 (VLAN 10) with 0%
loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing is healthy in both
directions and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces
the VLAN20->VLAN10 path (Laptop0 -> PC4), finds it working, checks router0's
sub-interfaces, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped eth0.20
sub-interface or a VLAN 20 -> VLAN 10 ACL to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The user's complaint that Laptop0 (172.16.20.10) is blocked from reaching
the 172.16.10.x segment (PC4, PC5, and other workstations) is not supported
by any evidence in the live network. Direct probes from laptop0 to all named
destinations — the inter-VLAN gateway (172.16.10.1), PC4 (172.16.10.4), and
PC5 (172.16.10.5) — all returned 0% packet loss with normal round-trip times.
The inter-VLAN routing path is router0, which has VLAN subinterfaces
eth0.10 (172.16.10.1/24) and eth0.20 (172.16.20.1/24) both UP, and
mswitch1 correctly bridges VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 traffic to the router on the
trunk link. Inspection of router0's iptables shows all three chains (INPUT,
FORWARD, OUTPUT) at policy ACCEPT with zero filter rules — there is no ACL,
no firewall rule, and no route-map in the FRR RIP configuration that could
be restricting traffic in either direction. The user's perception of being
"banned" or "blocked" does not correspond to any actual network fault.
Root cause: there is no fault; the network is operating correctly and
connectivity between the 172.16.20.x and 172.16.10.x subnets is fully
functional. No corrective action is required; the ticket should be closed as
a false alarm, and the user should be advised to retest their application
directly rather than assuming an infrastructure block.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verifies eth0.10 and eth0.20 are up, finds no inter-VLAN ACL/firewall, and shows Laptop0 reaches PC4 with 0% loss, matching the baseline-healthy note.
